title: Super Investors Are Changing Strategies
creator: Joseph Carlson After Hours
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions
summary: Joseph Carlson walks through the latest 13F filings of seven super investors — Valley Forge's Dev Kantesaria, Chris Hohne, Berkshire Hathaway, Josh Tarasoff and Pat Dorsey — and finds several shifting strategy after recent sell-offs. Kantesaria's fund has suffered multi-year underperformance as FICO fell from $2,400 to $700, yet he trimmed Mastercard by 84% and Moody's by 30% to fund new buys in Amazon, Broadcom, Nvidia and TSM; Carlson agrees with the Amazon buy, calling it an excellent buy at $257 and his top pick going into 2026, likes the TSM buy for its wide moat and low valuation, but notes the Nvidia and Broadcom buys likely came just before the drop. Tarasoff sold his Netflix position entirely, which Carlson disagrees with, and Dorsey's big buys in Veeva and Tyler Technologies plus adds to Meta, Booking and Uber impress him. Carlson then stresses that Jensen Huang's resignation is serious and material — Huang lobbied for China chip sales, Nvidia reported $12.4bn of China revenue, and a return is very unlikely — and cheers Amazon casting Robert Pattinson as James Bond under Denis Villeneuve. He closes by mocking AI doomer Jacob Coxon, who warns humanity will be annihilated by AI yet refuses to sell his OpenAI shares because he 'likes money'. Calls: AMZN BUY @ $257 (flip from HOLD), NVDA BUY reiterated, TSM BUY (flip from HOLD), AVGO UNCERTAIN, NFLX UNCERTAIN. Note: captions garble some names (Hohne/Hoare, Villeneuve) and one passage about a holding dumped at a loss could not be verified as a ticker.
